title: Fuchs Uveitis Syndrome in Depth

steps.tx: **Fuchs uveitis syndrome** is chronic unilateral low grade anterior uveitis with diffuse stellate keratic precipitates, iris atrophy and heterochromia, vitreous opacities and no posterior synechiae despite years of inflammation. It presents through cataract or floaters rather than pain, often discovered at routine examination. Bilateral asymmetric cases exist but unilateral teaching dominates examinations.
steps.say: Chronic quiet unilateral inflammation together gives Fuchs pattern through cataract presentation in adults characteristically over years. Stellate distribution gives precipitate clue additionally. Synechiae absence gives paradox sign.

steps.tx: **Iris atrophy** in Fuchs is diffuse stromal loss lightening colour and blurring crypt architecture, with heterochromia less obvious in dark irides where atrophy texture substitutes colour change.
